body.statement:
For fixed \(h\in\mathcal H\), define the open hard cells \(D_{\mathbf a}(h)=\{z:\ a_j\text{ is the unique maximizer of }R(h_j+z_j)\text{ for every }j\}\), their hard levels \(L_{\mathbf a}(h)=\sum_jp_j[\max_r(Rh_j)_r-(Rh_j)_{a_j}]\), and \(U_h(z)=\sup_{0<t\le1}G(h,z)(t)\).  Then every atom of \(S(h,Z_V)\) is at one of the finitely many values \(L_{\mathbf a}(h)\), and
\[
 P\{S(h,Z_V)=q\}=\sum_{\mathbf a:L_{\mathbf a}(h)=q}P\{Z_V\in D_{\mathbf a}(h),\ U_h(Z_V)\le q\}.
\]
The frozen assumptions do not imply a uniform atom-removed modulus.  In particular, there are legal fixed inputs with \(J=K=2\), \(p=(1/2,1/2)\), common benchmark \(b=(64/65,1/65)\), \(\beta=1/65\), \(\mathcal H=[1,5/4]^2\), and \(\mathcal K_V=\{I_2\}\), constants \(\eta>0\), and sequences \(h_m\in\mathcal H\), \(q_m\in\mathbb R\), and \(x_m\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 P\{q_m<S(h_m,Z_{I_2})\le q_m+x_m\}\ge\eta.
\]
Consequently no \(A(x)\downarrow0\) having the requested uniform property follows in general, even after the atom at \(q\) is removed.  The one-sided probability certificate of \(\mathsf A\) remains valid, including at all enumerated atoms, but the frozen assumptions alone do not supply a two-sided least-favorable quantile bracket of prescribed value width.
body.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 F_c(h,z)=(1+c)\sum_{j=1}^Jp_j\ell_{c,b_j}(Rh_j,Rz_j),
 \qquad 0<c<\infty,
\]
and let \(F_\infty(h,z)=G(h,z)(1)\). By the hard-endpoint lemma and the definition of the compactified path, on \(D_{\mathbf a}(h)\),
\[
 G(h,z)(0)=L_{\mathbf a}(h),\qquad
 \lim_{c\downarrow0}F_c(h,z)=L_{\mathbf a}(h),\qquad
 S(h,z)=\max\{L_{\mathbf a}(h),U_h(z)\}.                 \tag{1}
\]
The benchmark-support and stratum-mass assumptions give \(b_{ja}>0\) and \(p_j>0\) for every \(j,a\).

We first locate all possible atoms. Fix \(v\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\) and \(s>0\). Differentiating the finite sum in the definition of \(F_c\), using \(Dq_{c,b}(w)=c^{-1}C\{q_{c,b}(w)\}\), gives
\[
 \frac{d}{ds}F_c(h,sv)
 =\frac{s(1+c)}{c}\sum_{j=1}^Jp_j
 (Rv_j)^{\top}C\{q_{c,b_j}(R(h_j+sv_j))\}Rv_j.          \tag{2}
\]
Every coordinate of the Gibbs vector is positive. For a positive probability vector \(r\), \(x^{\top}C(r)x\) is the variance of the coordinates of \(x\) under \(r\), and hence vanishes exactly when those coordinates are constant. Since some \(v_j\ne0\), the vector \(Rv_j=(0,v_j^{\top})^{\top}\) is not constant. Thus (2) is strictly positive. At the quadratic endpoint, the matrix inequality in the high-endpoint lemma similarly yields
\[
 \frac{d}{ds}F_\infty(h,sv)
 =s\sum_{j=1}^Jp_jv_j^{\top}R^{\top}C(b_j)Rv_j
 \ge s\beta^2\sum_{j=1}^Jp_j\|v_j\|_2^2>0.             \tag{3}
\]

The intersection of \(D_{\mathbf a}(h)\) with a ray \(\{sv:s>0\}\) is an interval because it is the intersection of finitely many strict affine inequalities in \(s\). Suppose \(s_1<s_2\) belong to that interval and \(U_h(s_1v)>L_{\mathbf a}(h)\). Compactified path continuity and (1) imply that the supremum defining \(U_h(s_1v)\) is attained at some \(t_*\in(0,1]\). Equations (2)--(3), at the corresponding finite or infinite temperature, then give
\[
 U_h(s_2v)\ge G(h,s_2v)(t_*)>G(h,s_1v)(t_*)=U_h(s_1v). \tag{4}
\]
Also \(U_h(sv)\ge L_{\mathbf a}(h)\) by the first limit in (1). Therefore, for every \(q\ne L_{\mathbf a}(h)\), each radial section of
\[
 D_{\mathbf a}(h)\cap\{z:U_h(z)=q\}                  \tag{5}
\]
contains at most one point and has one-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero. Polar Fubini applied to (5) shows that (5) is Lebesgue null. The finitely many decision boundaries are affine hyperplanes. Since \(V\in\mathcal K_V\subset\mathbb S_{++}^d\), \(Z_V\) has a Lebesgue density, so those boundaries and (5) are Gaussian null.

Outside the decision boundaries, the hard cells partition \(\mathbb R^d\). On a cell with \(L_{\mathbf a}(h)>q\), (1) makes \(\{S=q\}\) empty. On a cell with \(L_{\mathbf a}(h)<q\), that event is contained in the null set (5). On a cell with \(L_{\mathbf a}(h)=q\), (1) gives the exact equivalence
\[
 \{S(h,Z_V)=q\}\cap\{Z_V\in D_{\mathbf a}(h)\}
 =\{Z_V\in D_{\mathbf a}(h),\ U_h(Z_V)\le q\}.       \tag{6}
\]
Summing (6) over the \(K^J\) cells proves both the displayed atom formula and the assertion that no other atom is possible.

We next construct the collision witness. Set
\[
 r=\frac{b_1}{b_0}=\frac1{64},\qquad
 \mathcal H_0=[1,5/4]^2,
\]
and write the augmented binary true reward as \((0,h)\). At error \(z=-2h\), the estimated reward is \((0,-h)\). With \(x=h/c\), direct substitution in the log-sum-exp formula gives
\[
 \frac{\ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,-2h)\}}{h}
 =1+\frac1x\log\frac{r+e^{-x}}{1+re^{-x}}
   -\frac{2re^{-x}}{1+re^{-x}}.                       \tag{7}
\]
We prove, uniformly for \(1\le h\le5/4\), that
\[
 (1+c)\ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,-2h)\}<h,qquad c>0.       \tag{8}
\]
If \(0<x\le2\), then along the segment from \((0,h)\) to \((0,-h)\) the action-one odds are at most \(re^x\). The integral representation in the Bregman-identity lemma therefore gives
\[
 \ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,-2h)\}
 \le \frac{4h^2}{c}\int_0^1sre^x\,ds
 =2hxr e^x.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \frac{(1+c)\ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,-2h)\}}h
 \le2re^x(x+h)\le\frac{13e^2}{128}<1,                \tag{9}
\]
where the last strict inequality follows from \(e<3\). If \(x\ge2\), put
\[
 D(x)=\log\frac{1+re^{-x}}{r+e^{-x}}.
\]
Its derivative is
\[
 D'(x)=\frac{e^{-x}(1-r^2)}{(r+e^{-x})(1+re^{-x})}>0. \tag{10}
\]
Moreover, \(e^2>7\) and \(e^{5/4}<4\) imply
\[
 D(2)>\log4>\frac54\ge h.                             \tag{11}
\]
Indeed, \(r+e^{-2}<1/64+1/7<1/4\), while the numerator in \(D(2)\) exceeds one. Rewriting (7) now yields
\[
 \ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,-2h)\}
 =h-cD(x)-\frac{2hre^{-x}}{1+re^{-x}}<h(1-c).
\]
Here \(c=h/x\le5/8<1\), and hence
\[
 (1+c)\ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,-2h)\}<h(1-c^2)<h.
\]
This completes the proof of (8). All numerical inequalities in (9)--(11) follow, for example, from the positive-term exponential series and the geometric remainder bound.

For \(h=(h_1,h_2)\in\mathcal H_0\), define
\[
 z^{(1)}(h)=(-2h_1,0),\qquad z^{(2)}(h)=(0,-2h_2).
\]
At \(z^{(k)}(h)\), exactly stratum \(k\) chooses the wrong hard action, so its hard level is
\[
 L_k(h)=p_kh_k=\frac{h_k}{2}.                          \tag{12}
\]
Equation (8) proves \(F_c\{h,z^{(k)}(h)\}<L_k(h)\) for every finite \(c>0\). We now verify that this inequality persists on an open neighborhood uniformly over all temperatures and all \(h\in\mathcal H_0\).

Choose a fixed neighborhood small enough that the estimated contrast in the wrong stratum is at most \(-\kappa\) and that in the correct stratum is at least \(\kappa\), for some \(\kappa>0\) independent of \(h\). For a scalar perturbation \(z\), put \(w=h+z\). The exact binary formula
\[
 \ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,z)\}
 =c\log\frac{1+re^{h/c}}{1+re^{w/c}}
   +z\frac{re^{w/c}}{1+re^{w/c}}                     \tag{13}
\]
and \(0\le\log(1+y)\le y\) give, uniformly in that neighborhood as \(c\downarrow0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (1+c)\ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,z)\}
 &=h+c(h+\log r)+c^2\log r
   +O\!\left((1+c)(c+|z|)r^{-1}e^{-\kappa/c}\right)
 &&(w\le-\kappa),\\
 (1+c)\ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,z)\}
 &=O\!\left((1+c)(c+|z|)r^{-1}e^{-\kappa/c}\right)
 &&(w\ge\kappa).
 \end{aligned}                                        \tag{14}
\]
Since \(h+\log r\le5/4-\log64<0\), the negative term linear in \(c\) in the wrong stratum dominates the two exponentially small remainders in (14). Thus there are \(c_0>0\) and a uniform neighborhood of each \(z^{(k)}(h)\) on which \(F_c(h,z)<L_k(h)\) for \(0<c\le c_0\).

On every compact interval \([c_0,C_0]\), (8), continuity, and compactness of \([1,5/4]^2\times[c_0,C_0]\) give a strictly positive uniform margin at the central points; uniform continuity extends it to a common neighborhood. At the remaining endpoint, the high-temperature lemma gives uniform convergence to
\[
 F_\infty\{h,z^{(k)}(h)\}
 =\frac12p_k(2h_k)^2b_0b_1
 =b_0b_1h_k^2<\frac{h_k}{2}=L_k(h),                   \tag{15}
\]
because \(2b_0b_1h_k<1\). Its explicit \(O(c^{-1})\) remainder, followed by uniform continuity on a bounded neighborhood, supplies \(C_0<\infty\) and the same strict inequality for \(c\ge C_0\). Combining the small, compact-intermediate, and large temperature ranges yields a number \(\delta>0\), independent of \(h\), such that the open cubes
\[
 B_k(h)=\{z:\|z-z^{(k)}(h)\|_\infty<\delta\},\qquad k=1,2,                \tag{16}
\]
remain in the corresponding hard cell and satisfy
\[
 S(h,z)=L_k(h)\quad\text{for every }z\in B_k(h).       \tag{17}
\]

The centers in (16) range over a compact set. The standard bivariate Gaussian density is therefore bounded below by a positive constant on the union of the closures of smaller concentric cubes. Their Lebesgue volumes are fixed and positive, so for some \(\eta>0\),
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_0}P\{Z_{I_2}\in B_k(h)\}\ge\eta,
 \qquad k=1,2.                                        \tag{18}
\]

Let \(\delta_m\downarrow0\), set
\[
 h_m=(1,1+\delta_m),\qquad q_m=\frac12,
 \qquad x_m=\frac{\delta_m}{2}.
\]
By (12), the first atom is at the excluded left endpoint \(q_m\), while the second is at \(q_m+x_m\). Equations (17)--(18) give
\[
 P\{q_m<S(h_m,Z_{I_2})\le q_m+x_m\}
 \ge P\{Z_{I_2}\in B_2(h_m)\}\ge\eta.               \tag{19}
\]

For completeness, these fixed inputs arise from legal causal laws. Draw \(X\) uniformly on two strata and \(A\) uniformly and independently conditional on \(X\). Conditional on \(X=j\), take independent potential-outcome residuals with values \(\pm1/(2\sqrt2)\), and set
\[
 Y(0)=\epsilon_0,qquad Y(1)=\frac{h_j}{\sqrt n}+\epsilon_1,
 \qquad Y=Y(A).
\]
Rows are i.i.d.; consistency and conditional randomization hold by construction; \(|Y(a)|<2\); the stratum and action probabilities equal \(1/2\); the benchmark support equals \(1/65\); and the local remainder is zero. Each residual variance is \(1/8\), so the contrast-score variance in stratum \(j\) is
\[
 \frac1{p_j}\left(\frac{1/8}{e_{j1}}+\frac{1/8}{e_{j0}}\right)
 =2\left(\frac14+\frac14\right)=1.                  \tag{20}
\]
Scores from different strata have zero product, hence \(V_n=I_2\). Thus every law used by (19) belongs to the declared model class.

If a uniform atom-removed modulus \(A(x)\downarrow0\) followed from the frozen assumptions, applying it to (19) would give \(\eta\le A(x_m)\to0\), a contradiction. Finally, the certified-calibration theorem verifies a one-sided lower-CDF inequality directly and its fallback uses only a Gaussian tail bound. Neither step invokes a small-interval modulus. Its certificate therefore remains valid at the atoms characterized in (6), whereas a two-sided conversion from probability error to a prescribed critical-value width is unavailable under the frozen assumptions alone.
body.justification: The theorem identifies all hard-cell atoms, proves a fixed legal collision witness, and supplies the counterexample used for upward negative class transfer.
body.gap: Standard Gaussian anti-concentration does not cover this nonlinear supremum, and the collision proves that a vanishing atom-removed modulus is false rather than merely unproved.
body.consumer: Implementers retain atom-safe one-sided calibration while recognizing that prescribed two-sided value accuracy needs additional structure.
